title: Reading Drill — Measuring a pond's change in level — Building a comparison
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Measuring a pond's change in level — Building a comparison
passages.body:
**A** The park ecologist had been asked to investigate still water on the shore hiding a slow rise in Foxhaven. Its first task was to decide which signs of improvement could be compared between sites. It settled on water depth beside the outlet, because the same measure could be applied in the original setting and at a second location.

**B** During a five-week comparison, the team used a gauge board at both places. It recorded outcomes separately for each site. Because recent watering nearby might influence the figures, the team used a column in the record to show when that condition was present. The surveys included quiet periods as well as busy ones.

**C** The team then put forward readings at fixed intervals. Its report asked for another comparison after the change had been tried. This would distinguish a genuine effect from an improvement that could have occurred anyway. The report did not assume that the more successful site before the change would be the better site afterwards.
